name: pixeldosa-agent-guide
title: Pixel Dosa Agent Guide
description: An instruction file for AI coding agents building with Pixel Dosa, installed into a team's repository so their agent knows not just which component to use but how to use it well. Covers registry setup, a job-to-component selection table, when to start from a Block instead of assembling parts, the non-negotiable UX rules (nothing commits silently, never add Accept all, approvals phrased as consequences with reversibility and impact stated, nothing waiting on the user is animated, shimmer only on active status verbs, a visible Stop during every working state, no faked typing, confidence as tiers not percentages), a mapping table from common agent events to component states, and a pre-finish checklist. Installs as a Claude Code skill; other agents can be pointed at the same file or at the site's llms.txt. Contains no code and adds no dependencies.
docs: Installs to .claude/skills/pixeldosa/SKILL.md, where Claude Code discovers it automatically. For Cursor, Copilot, or other agents, reference this file from your rules or AGENTS.md, or point the agent at https://pixeldosa.akshayjayan.com/llms.txt.

meta.engineeringNotes: Coding agents already find and install Pixel Dosa through the shadcn MCP server and CLI search, because every registry description was written for cold LLM comprehension. What they could not do was use the components well: nothing stopped an agent from wiring an AI value straight into data or adding an Accept all button, since those decisions live in the design system's judgment rather than its props. This item transfers that judgment into the consumer's repository as a plain markdown skill, so the rules travel with the code instead of staying on a docs site the agent may never read. It is the same source the site's llms.txt draws its rules from, so the two cannot drift. It ships as registry:file with no dependencies, consistent with the principle that Pixel Dosa never requires an agent stack.
meta.motionNotes: No motion — this item is a documentation file, not a component. It does, however, carry the system's motion rules to agents in written form: motion means the machine is busy and stillness means it is the user's turn, shimmer is reserved for active status verbs, completed text is never revealed character by character, and prefers-reduced-motion is always respected rather than overridden.
